description:
PROBLEM
People who put savings into DeFi get better yield, plus a second job: watching dashboards, reading risk updates and signing transactions at midnight. Risk changes while they sleep. The alternatives are worse: bots and AI agents that want your private keys and full control, with nothing to stop them when they get it wrong at 3 AM.

SOLUTION
KRIYA is an autonomous capital protocol on Monad. You stop programming transactions and program a financial objective instead: a mandate with a goal ("maximise risk-adjusted yield") and hard limits (max risk, max exposure per strategy, minimum reserve, max drawdown). The mandate lives in a smart contract. From then on a loop runs without anyone clicking a button:

1. OBSERVE: a Chainlink CRE workflow reads an external risk feed (HTTP + consensus) and every mandate's onchain state.
2. VERIFY: changed risk scores are written onchain as a signed CRE report (KriyaExecutor.onReport → strategy registry).
3. DETECT: every mandate is re-evaluated against the verified risk.
4. DECIDE: an AI agent (Claude) proposes a typed allocation; a deterministic optimizer is the fallback.
5. CONSTRAIN: the same policy engine, compiled into the CRE WASM, re-checks the proposal.
6. EXECUTE: a signed CRE report moves the funds; the contracts check the mandate again, so anything outside it reverts.

AI proposes, rules constrain, Chainlink verifies, smart contracts enforce. Even a wrong or malicious agent cannot move funds outside the user's mandate.

WHAT IT DID ON MONAD TESTNET (all real transactions)
- A $1,000 test-USDC mandate (max risk 40, max 40% per strategy, 25% reserve).
- Strategy B's verified risk jumped 34 → 48. Chainlink CRE wrote it onchain (0x4789f3eb…97de) and, in the same workflow run 16 blocks / ~5 s later, rebalanced the mandate out of B (0x58557a0a…7d0b): 400 USDC moved to safety, portfolio risk 14/40.
- An unsafe proposal (60% into one strategy) was rejected by the contract onchain with ExposureExceeded (0xe8c15294…9466).

WHY MONAD
400 ms blocks mean a verified risk change and the rebalance that answers it land seconds apart, so a mandate spends almost no time outside its limits. Nearly gasless execution makes it practical to check every rule onchain on every allocation (a full CRE rebalance cost 0.15 MON on testnet). Full EVM compatibility let the same Solidity, Foundry tests and Chainlink CRE workflow run unchanged; the CRE CLI targets monad-testnet natively. The app also handles Monad's 100-block eth_getLogs cap with an incremental event-log index.

BUILT WITH
Solidity 0.8.26 + Foundry (23 tests incl. fuzz properties), OpenZeppelin, Chainlink CRE TypeScript SDK (WASM workflow, signed reports into a ReceiverTemplate), Next.js 16 + React 19 + wagmi/viem dashboard, Claude API, Upstash Redis, Vercel.

Contracts (Monad testnet, chain 10143): KriyaExecutor 0x9c5f1A2326Fa1C16e04Ecf32C60091150161656A · KriyaVault 0xd167B393646E39A01bB14A4e0C53A96940C249ee · KriyaMandate 0x97FD1b5af7622377744C8c2F44F4fF3A04a52073 · KriyaStrategyRegistry 0xadAE9Abccf4fE599405C39bC19A4686566dEd7b6.

Roadmap: cross-chain mandates via Chainlink CCIP, real Monad DeFi protocols as strategies, Safe-module mandates for DAO treasuries.
gtm:
FIRST USERS
1. Individuals with stablecoins in DeFi who want yield without the night shift: crypto-native professionals (starting with India's large developer and crypto community) who already use lending pools and LP vaults but can't monitor them 24/7.
2. Small DAO treasuries and community funds that hold idle stablecoins, need written rules (mandates) and can't afford one bad night.
3. Crypto funds and treasury ops teams that want policy-enforced automation instead of trusting a bot with keys.

HOW WE REACH THEM
- Monad ecosystem first: launch on Monad with mandate templates for Monad-native lending and LP protocols, integrate those protocols as KRIYA strategies, and co-market with them (their users become our users; KRIYA brings them sticky, rule-bound TVL).
- Chainlink and Monad developer communities: open-source workflow + contracts, demos at community calls and hackathons, so builders can add their own strategies.
- DAO treasuries: a Safe-module version so a DAO can adopt a mandate through a normal governance proposal; outreach via treasury-management forums and DAO tooling partners.
- Story-led content: "sleep through the risk" short videos showing real onchain rebalances and reverted unsafe proposals; every action is verifiable on the explorer, which is the trust hook.
- Low-friction onboarding: connect a wallet, pick a template mandate, deposit; no keys handed to anyone.

BUSINESS MODEL
A small management fee in basis points on assets under mandate, and later a performance fee on yield above a benchmark. Monad's low fees keep frequent onchain enforcement affordable even for small mandates, which opens the long tail of retail users.
judge:
1. Open the live demo mandate (no wallet needed): https://kriya-monad.vercel.app/?view=0x09855cE865D094F6c2F2B5A13F64FC6F82b3B4C7
2. The Autonomous Loop panel shows the last Chainlink CRE run step by step; the Activity feed links every onchain step (CRE risk report, CRE rebalance, reverted guardrail test) to the Monad explorer.
3. Press "Preview decision" to get a live allocation from Claude, re-checked by the policy engine (nothing is written onchain).
4. To program your own mandate: connect a wallet on Monad testnet (get MON from https://faucet.monad.xyz); the app mints test USDC.
5. CRE evidence: https://github.com/Saurabhnage/kriya/blob/main/docs/CRE_SIMULATION.md (broadcast runs on monad-testnet with CRE CLI v1.38).
